title: Decode Railway: latency vs cost exploratory notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note exploring an alternate framing for decode-path optimizations — I call it the "Decode Railway" experiment set. Aim is to compare three practical families:
  1) Baseline dynamic batching (what we currently serve most requests with)
  2) Proactive KV-prefetch (small prefix prefetch + cached KV reuse)
  3) Compact decode pipeline (shorter attention windows + 4-bit quantized kernel + early-exit heuristics)

Testbed summary (quick, approximate):
- Model: small-to-midsize open decoder (13B-like architecture emulation). No RLHF artifacts; standard causal LM.
- Hardware: A100-40GB (v2-equivalent) nodes for steady-state; single-run on H100-80GB for sanity check.
- Workload mixes: 
  A) Conversational micro-turns: 1-3 tokens per reply (but many back-and-forth, session affinity).
  B) Short generation: 32-64 tokens per request (single-shot instructions).
  C) Long finishers: 256 tokens avg (rare but costy).
- Arrival patterns: Poisson baseline; synthetic spike windows (10s ramp to 5x qps).
- Metric set: p50/p90/p95 latency (ms), tail (p99), tokens/sec throughput, dollars per 10k tokens (approx infra + amortized overhead).

Methodology notes (rough):
- All runs instrumented with trace IDs to join Console export (see linked PR).
- Cost model: amortized GPU minute cost + storage of KV cache memory pressure mapped to slot occupancy. Not accounting for network egress.
- Each scenario run 3x, median reported; spike runs include cold-starts for 50% of sessions.

ASCII result summary (median of medians, illustrative — replace with raw numbers in final):

Scenario              | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | tokens/sec | $/10k tokens
----------------------+--------+--------+--------+------------+------------
Baseline dyn-batch     |  60    | 180    | 520    |   1200     |  3.20
KV-prefetch (small)    |  45    | 140    | 380    |   1350     |  2.90
Compact decode (4-bit) |  40    | 130    | 420    |   1600     |  1.95

Quick observations from table:
- Compact decode shows the best cost/token (approx 40% lower than baseline) primarily due to quantized kernel speedups and lower memory traffic.
- KV-prefetch reduces p99 substantially versus baseline in conversational micro-turns but gains shrink for long finishers because prefetch useful prefix fraction is small.
- Compact decode p99 sometimes worse than KV-prefetch; hypothesized cause: early-exit heuristics misfire on rare long-context patterns, causing slower fallbacks.

Scenario breakdown (text charts):
1) Conversational micro-turns (many short sessions)
   - Baseline: bursts create slot contention; p95 spikes widely.
   - KV-prefetch: reduces slot occupancy by ~12% via reuse; p95 down ~20%.
   - Compact: throughput good, but p99 has fatter tail from a subset of sessions with long token histories where quantization causes decoding jitter.

2) Short generation (32-64 tokens)
   - Compact decode wins on cost and p50/p90.
   - KV-prefetch wins marginally on p99 when there is high session-locality (repeated prompts).

3) Long finishers (256 tokens)
   - Compact decode cost advantage persists but latency advantage diminishes; baseline is competitive on tail because batching amortizes kernel launch overhead.

Micro-chart: p95 spread across workload types (normalized, lower is better)
- Conversational:   Baseline=1.0 | KV-prefetch=0.8 | Compact=0.85
- Short-gen:       Baseline=1.0 | KV-prefetch=0.95| Compact=0.6
- Long-finisher:   Baseline=1.0 | KV-prefetch=0.98| Compact=0.9

Open issues / follow-ups (explicit):
- Re-run on H100 hardware to validate quantization kernels; current A100 results may under/overstate speedups. (linked artifact: GH PR 4987)
- Add memory pressure curve: how does KV-prefetch cache TTL affect slot churn and run-to-run variance?
- Investigate p99 causes in compact decode: instrument kernel-level stalls and early-exit thresholds; add micro-profiling at assembly/kernel boundaries.
- Validate cost model sensitivity to amortized slot overhead assumptions (+/- 20% changes).

Actionable next steps (short):
- [ ] Run focused microbench on H100 - single topology, isolate long-history sessions (owner: Arjun). Target: 2028-05-17.
- [ ] Add TTL sweep to KV-prefetch runs (owner: Sofia). Target: 2028-05-21.
- [ ] Add trace-level annotation for early-exit events (owner: Diego). Target: 2028-05-14.

Draft framing for external collateral (one-paragraph):
"Decode Railway" is a pragmatic set of decode-path experiments showing that combined algorithmic and kernel-level optimizations can materially reduce inference unit economics, especially for short and medium-length generation tasks. Our experiments show a tradeoff frontier: aggressive quantization and compact decoding drive cost down but require targeted instrumentation to avoid tail latency regressions in long-session workloads.

- Is the cost model conservative enough for enterprise billing? (I think yes but need finance sanity check)
- Which scenario should be prioritized for product-level feature gating? My bias: prioritize short-generation where cost wins and p99 risk low.
